notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation for Dedicated capacity. Primary ask: guaranteed throughput for low-latency financial chat + reranking pipeline. They run bursty spikes around market open/close and need predictable tail latency for SLAs to their internal customers.

Key perf targets discussed:
- Baseline min tokens/sec: they requested a contract-level guarantee of 12,000 tokens/sec aggregate for the pool (targets the core reranking + chat mix).
- Per-concurrency cap: proposal from Redwood was 50 concurrent streams per pool (can be tuned). Cobalt Nimbus pushed back, preferring 80 concurrent to support many small chat sessions concurrently.
- Burst policy: must support 2x burst for 10 minutes during market open and up to 5x for 60s microbursts. They want predictable throttling behaviour (queue vs reject) and transparent metrics.
- Latency SLOs: P95 generation latency target 250ms for chat (prompt avg 128 tokens), max acceptable P99 600ms. For reranking (short sequences) P95 120ms.
- Reserved GPU planning: preliminary sizing suggests 8x H100-equivalent GPUs to meet baseline with 40ms per-token perf numbers, but they want Redwood to map to a validated config (either 8x A100-80GB with advanced batching or 6x H100 depending on quantization).
- Auto-scaling and burst credits: they asked for a burst-credit bank (prepaid capacity) that can be drawn for scheduled spikes without triggering preemption.

Security & compliance notes:
- Must run in VPC with customer-managed KMS.
- Audit logs retained 1 year minimum.
- Data residency: EU market-sensitive dataset must stay in eu-west-1 for subset of workloads.

Commercial asks / SLA negotiation points:
- SLA credits: they want clear credit bands tied to throughput shortfalls (e.g., if throughput < 90% of guaranteed for a monthly window, 10% credit; <80% then 20%).
- Measurement window: propose 5-minute windows for burst evaluation, monthly rolling for baseline. They want both per-minute and per-hour telemetry.
- Term: 12- to 24-month reserved commitment; pricing needs GPU-equivalent unit + tokens overage.

Open technical questions:
- How does Redwood measure "tokens/sec" across mixed models and seq lengths? Need agreed benchmark harness (we proposed a synthetic traffic mix mirroring their production mixture).
- Priority and pre-emption policy when Dedicated pool is under contention (can fallback to slower model variants with auto-degradation?).
- Exact mapping from Redwood capacity units to their internal SLOs (they asked for a capacity planning spreadsheet).

CRM-style shorthand / recent touches:
- 2026-02-15: initial inbound (AE Jordan Park), requested pricing for reserved pool.
- 2026-02-22: tech deep-dive with SE Sofia M.; ran perf harness on sample model, preliminary numbers attached (drive link).
- 2026-03-03: security questionnaire submitted; SOC2 docs shared.
- 2026-03-08: call w/ eng + ops (ff-2026-03-08-74ab) — they emphasized burst policy and SLA credits; asked for written proposal.
- 2026-03-10: Redwood sent preliminary sizing + two commercial options (8x A100 path vs 6x H100 path).

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to provide capacity mapping spreadsheet and updated SLA language reflecting tokens/sec definition, measurement windows, and credit bands (owner: Jordan Park).
- SE to validate quantized model perf on proposed hardware and confirm burst sizing (owner: Sofia Martinez).
- Legal + procurement to review pricing addendum; customer to respond to final commercial by 2026-04-20.

Short quotes: "We need guarantees — not just averages. Market open minutes are our SLA moments." — VP Eng.

Stability / risk: High reward if SLA holds; risk if burst coverage insufficient leading to internal SLAs breach. Procurement timeline is main commercial risk.
